answer: Independence is billed. Each epoch an identity files two invoices from competing carriers for the same bytes, counted only when both meters agree at one interchange point and share no path. No uplink can be billed twice by rivals: a farm behind one pipe shows one volume however many keys it carries, and payout is capped per key. Carriers stamp flows with a signed beacon timestamp and lose their licence for certifying phantom traffic, so bought records expire. Honest agents ride the tide of their work; farms rent two lines per identity each epoch. A lone juniper bills what it sends.
